request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 2.)

tools.name: get_fold_detail
tools.description: Get the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown for a completed experiment run. Use this to compare fold-level consistency between runs.

output.text:
**Choice: run 4** (LightGBM, all+agent features, no imbalance handling). My confidence is moderate, about 0.6.

**Fold-by-fold PR-AUC (5 folds)**

| Run | F1 | F2 | F3 | F4 | F5 | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (lgbm, all) | 0.7818 | 0.7221 | 0.6295 | 0.7932 | 0.7285 | 0.731 |
| 2 (rf, no_size) | 0.7396 | 0.6692 | 0.5712 | 0.7676 | 0.6878 | 0.687 |
| 3 (lgbm, all+agent, class weight) | 0.7753 | 0.6942 | 0.6201 | 0.8069 | 0.7245 | 0.724 |
| 4 (lgbm, all+agent) | 0.7813 | 0.7324 | 0.6391 | 0.7874 | 0.7341 | 0.735 |
| 5 (lgbm, no_size) | 0.7942 | 0.6761 | 0.6027 | 0.7905 | 0.6983 | 0.712 |

- **Fold wins:** Run 4 has the best score in 3 of 5 folds (F2, F3, F5). Run 5 wins F1 and run 3 wins F4.
- **Head-to-head with run 1:** Run 4 wins 3 of 5 folds. It loses F1 by 0.0005 and F4 by about 0.006.
- **Consistency:** Run 4 also has the lowest spread (SD 0.059) and the best mean, precision@50 and ROC-AUC.
- **Complexity:** Run 4 uses the same hyperparameters as run 1 and only adds the agent features. Class weighting (run 3) didn't help, and the random forest is clearly worse.

**Caveats**
- **Small margin:** The gap between run 4 and run 1 is about 0.004 PR-AUC. That is well inside the fold SD of about 0.06, so the two are effectively tied. A 3-of-5 fold win is weak evidence.
- **Fold difficulty:** The folds differ far more than the models do. F3 is around 0.60–0.64 for every run, and F4 is around 0.79–0.81.
- **ROC-AUC of about 0.94:** This is high for a label of unknown origin. If the label comes from a rule or a prior audit, the model may be learning that process instead of fraud. The "agent" features need a leakage check, as does anything that reflects claim volume, which the no_size variants hint at. The no_size runs lose only a little, which suggests size isn't the whole story.
- **Time split:** The claims cover only about 13 months. I can't tell whether the folds are time-ordered or random, so temporal leakage is possible.
- **Queue size:** Precision@50 of about 0.78 is the more relevant number for a queue of about 100. It is still measured against suspicion labels, not confirmed fraud.

I'm stopping the search. The configurations are within noise of each other, and another round of tuning is unlikely to help. Checking the agent features and the label origin would help more.

**Final: chosen_run = 4, stop = true, confidence ≈ 0.6.**
